items_missed: 1_set_agenda: No 'how are you today,' no agenda statement (what we'll cover + time estimate), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
2_probe: No zip codes confirmed for either address, no question about additional storage needs or narrow hallways/tight turns, no explicit moving-stressors question.
3_pricing: Inclusions list skipped gas and wrap pads/bands explicitly (truck, taxes, insurance, CC fees, assembly/disassembly were covered).
4_clock: Never stated the 15-minute prorated increment after the minimum, and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check on the clock policy.
5_estimate: Destination's 3rd-floor/no-elevator stairs (gathered during probing) were never tied back in as a time variable when presenting the estimate.
6_save_your_ass: Entire prep speech missing — no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill,' no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no close.
7_quote_booking: No explicit 'no deposit required,' didn't mention a bolded detail list at the top of the email, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go,' no hours/how-to-reach-us given.
8_politeness: Used the customer's name only once ('hi Hunter') instead of 3+ times.
9_bonus: No mention of the 60 cents/lb baseline valuation alongside No Worries coverage.
top_strength: Pricing and differentiators were strong and complete — Joanna hit all three tracked differentiators in one breath (No Worries damage coverage up to $2,000, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and gave Hunter a clear, itemized price range ($1,129 to $1,429) tied to hours. She also handled a mid-call dropped connection gracefully ('it's actually my minute, I'm so sorry about that'), and Hunter, a repeat customer, closed the call visibly happy: 'I love it, I love it... real comfortable with you all.'
coaching_note: The Save Your Ass prep speech is completely missing from this call — add it every time, it's the highest-value section for shortening moves and lowering the customer's bill, and it's a full 10 points you're leaving on the table. Open with a real agenda statement (what you'll cover, how long it'll take, 'sound good?') instead of jumping straight into confirming details. Close stronger too: state no deposit is required, ask if there are any other questions before you let them go, and give hours/contact info. Use Hunter's name a few more times through the call — you only said it once.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently patient and warm language (especially recovering from the dropped call), and the customer's own words at close ('I love it, I love it,' 'real comfortable with you all') confirm genuine comfort and rapport.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled by ASR errors throughout (mangled phrases like 'twenty half hour min' and 'all the Ros', plus a mid-call dropped connection), which limits confidence in reading tone from text alone despite the customer's clearly positive reaction.
